title: Capstone: a small collection
hook: your house hooks for your chosen toy yarn
yarn: your chosen toy yarn in a planned palette (24/7 Cotton or what your scale table favors)
summary: Three related original toys, one taken all the way through testing, tech editing and free publication, then a portfolio and a public review.
intro: No toy credential exists, so the capstone is the real thing: a pattern strangers can follow. You design three related originals, take one through testers and an outside tech edit, and publish it free. Then you build a portfolio from your first kit to now, and ask for outside eyes to set your next goal.
outcomes: You can design a set of toys that share a theme and a construction idea.
You can run a public pattern test and act on every tester question.
You can publish a versioned pattern with clear terms and credits.
You can present your work and turn critique into one next goal.
assessment: T490.1 passes on rubric scores for all three toys, a matching second copy, three finished tester toys, resolved tech-edit notes and a public, versioned pattern. T490.2 passes on a complete portfolio and logged outside comments. The Amigurumi.com contest entry is optional and not scored.
reading: The Essential Guide to Amigurumi (June Gilbank), Part 3, Designing Amigurumi, reread start to finish before Stage 1.

units.time: about 40 to 60 hours over 3 to 6 months
units.why: Three related originals show a style, where a single toy can be luck. Taking one of them all the way through testing, tech editing and publishing is the honest equivalent of a degree project, because no toy credential exists.
units.need: Your style sheet (T420.1), self tech-edit checklist and count spreadsheet (T420.2), toy yarn in your chosen palette, hooks, Poly-Fil, eyes or embroidery thread, a ruler, a kitchen scale in grams, a phone camera with your photo setup (T420.4), the toy rubric, a Ravelry or Ribblr account.
units.learn: Free: Elise Rose, How to Become an Amigurumi Designer in 8 Easy Steps, for the whole path in one post. Testers: r/PatternTesting (Reddit). Publishing: Ribblr's interactive patterns or a free Ravelry pattern page. Terms of use model: June Gilbank, PlanetJune terms of use. Photos: Sweet Softies, Essential Crochet Photography Tips (July 2026). Paid, only if you want a trained editor's eye: The Tech Editor Hub, Learn to Tech Edit Crochet (seven weeks; price not seen as of Oct 2026), or hire one tech edit for this pattern (rates vary; ask for a quote). Textbook: June Gilbank, The Essential Guide to Amigurumi, Part 3. Left-handed: No left-handed version; mirror the right-handed steps.
key: A collection shares a theme and one construction idea, such as three woodland animals on the same body, or three sea creatures with the same fin method.
Design all three on paper first, then make them one at a time. Reuse your best part between them where it fits.
Only one of the three goes through the full pipeline. The other two are finished toys with written round tables.
Testing: recruit at least 3 testers, ideally including one left-handed maker and one at the lowest skill level you list. Ask each for photos, measurements and every question they had.
Tech edit: run your T420.2 self-edit first, then one outside edit, either paid or swapped with another designer.
Publish free with a version number and a dated errata line. Credit any designer whose technique you adapted.
drill: Stage 1, plan (about 4 h): write the theme, the shared construction idea, and a front and side sketch at actual size for all three toys, each broken into parts with counts.
Stage 2, make (about 25 h): make toy 1, writing the round table as you go. Score it on the rubric. Then toy 2, then toy 3, each with its own round table.
Stage 3, pick one (about 1 h): choose the toy whose pattern is clearest. Make a second copy from your written pattern alone and compare each part within 3 mm.

Stage 4, write and self-edit (about 8 h): full pattern to your style sheet, yardage by weight (grams x your yarn's yards per gram, plus 15%), abbreviations, a safety note, terms of use. Recompute every count in your spreadsheet.
Stage 5, test (about 6 h of your time over 3 to 6 weeks): post a tester call with skill level, yarn, timeline and what you need back. Collect every question and photo.
Stage 6, revise and edit (about 4 h): fix every line a tester asked about. Send it for one outside tech edit. Apply the edits.
Stage 7, publish (about 2 h): publish free as version 1.0 with your own photos, the test credits and an errata line.
pass: All three toys score 12 or more of 16 on the toy rubric, with no 0 for Safety.
Your second copy of the chosen toy matches the first within 3 mm (1/8 in) on every part.
At least 3 testers finish the toy, and at least 2 of their finished toys are within 10% of your stated height in their photos with a ruler.
Every tester question has a matching change in the revision notes, and the outside edit's notes are all resolved or answered.
The pattern is public with a version number, a date and an errata line.
wrong: Testers' toys come out very different sizes
Your gauge note is unclear. State the finished height with the yarn and hook you used, and tell testers to go down a hook size if stuffing shows.
Common. Recruit one or two more than you need, and give a clear end date.
The third toy doesn't feel like the other two
Bring back the shared construction idea or the palette. Make the next version closer; keep this one as its own toy.
units.new_skill: Running one original from design through public testing, an outside tech edit and publishing

units.time: about 8 to 12 hours over 2 to 4 weeks
units.why: A portfolio shows how far you have come, from your first kit to your own published pattern. Outside eyes then give you one clear next goal. The major ends with a direction for your next toy.
units.need: Photos of your toys from across the major (your first toys Felix, Mort and Pierre, and your T190.1 and T290.1 pieces), your rubric scores and hours logs, your T490.1 collection, a free page or document to hold the portfolio.
units.learn: Optional contest: Amigurumi.com annual design contest (the 2025 theme was Rainbows with more than 7,500 voters; no 2026 theme was seen as of Oct 2026). For honest critique, post in r/Amigurumi or r/CrochetHelp using the app's Ask template. Photos: Daisy Cottage Designs, Crochet Photography Tips. Splurge, clearly optional, if you want to keep designing with a cohort: Garnknuten, Amigurumi Design LAB (about $289 as of Oct 2026; opens once a year). Left-handed: No left-handed version; mirror the right-handed steps.
key: Pick 10 to 12 toys. Show the range: a first toy, a multi-part toy, a face study, a texture toy, a doll, a structured toy, a remix, and the collection.
Pair one of your first toys with one recent toy of a similar shape. The pair tells the story without words.
Give each toy one line: its name, pattern or 'original', the skill it added, and its rubric score.
Ask about the toy: 'What one change would make this toy read better from across a room?'
Contest entries follow the contest's own rules for that year. Read them before you design for it.
drill: Photograph each chosen toy in your standard setup: same backdrop, light and angle.
Build the portfolio page: the toys in order, one line each, the first-and-recent pair, your total logged hours, and your rubric scores plotted over time.
Post the collection and the published pattern link in one community, with the Ask template and one specific question.
Log every reply. After a week, choose one change for your next design and write it as one sentence.
Optional: when the Amigurumi.com contest opens, enter one collection toy that fits its theme.
pass: The portfolio holds 10 or more toys, each with a photo, a one-line note and a rubric score.
It includes at least one first-and-recent pair of similar shapes.
You logged at least 3 outside comments and wrote one next-design goal from them.
wrong: No one replies to the post
Post once more at a different time of day with one clear question and a daylight photo. A reply count is not a measure of the toy.
Read it, wait a day, then pull out the one actionable line. Ignore anything about you rather than the toy.
units.new_skill: Presenting a body of work and turning outside critique into one goal
